headline.title: Tesla brings its robotaxi service to Dallas and Houston
headline.summary: Tesla has expanded its robotaxi service to Dallas and Houston, following its initial launch in Austin last year. The service now operates in three Texas cities, providing rides without safety drivers since January 2026.

articles.title: The RAM shortage could last years
articles.summary: A report from Nikkei Asia indicates that the global DRAM shortage may persist for several years, with suppliers projected to meet only 60 percent of demand by the end of 2027. SK Group's chairman has suggested that the shortages could extend until 2030, despite efforts by major memory manufacturers like Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron to increase production.

articles.title: Anthropic’s relationship with the Trump administration seems to be thawing
articles.summary: Anthropic continues to engage in discussions with senior officials from the Trump administration, despite being identified as a supply-chain risk by the Pentagon. The company's ongoing dialogue suggests a potential thawing of their previously strained relationship.

articles.title: It Takes 2 Minutes to Hack the EU’s New Age-Verification App
articles.summary: A recent report reveals that the European Union's new age-verification app can be hacked in just two minutes, raising concerns about its security measures. Additionally, significant data breaches have occurred at a gym chain and a hotel giant, alongside a disruptive DDoS attack on Bluesky.

articles.title: AI chip startup Cerebras files for IPO
articles.summary: AI chip startup Cerebras has filed for an initial public offering (IPO) following significant partnerships, including an agreement with Amazon Web Services to utilize its chips in data centers and a reported $10 billion deal with OpenAI. The IPO aims to capitalize on the growing demand for advanced AI hardware solutions.

articles.title: The App Store is booming again, and AI may be why
articles.summary: New data from Appfigures indicates a significant increase in app launches in 2026, suggesting that AI tools may be driving a resurgence in the mobile software market. This trend highlights the growing influence of AI technologies on app development and innovation.

articles.title: Schematik Is ‘Cursor for Hardware.’ Anthropic Wants In
articles.summary: Schematik is a new program designed to assist users in coding for physical devices, likened to a "cursor for hardware." Anthropic has expressed interest in the technology, which aims to simplify the coding process while ensuring safety.

articles.title: US-sanctioned currency exchange says $15 million heist done by "unfriendly states"
articles.summary: Grinex, a US-sanctioned currency exchange, claims that a recent $15 million heist was executed by "unfriendly states" with access to advanced hacking resources. The exchange's statement highlights concerns over the capabilities of state-sponsored cybercriminals.

articles.title: Sam Altman’s project World looks to scale its human verification empire. First stop: Tinder.
articles.summary: Sam Altman's project World is aiming to expand its human verification services through new partnerships, starting with Tinder. The initiative focuses on its Orb-centered anonymous verification system to enhance user safety and trust on platforms.

articles.title: OpenAI’s former Sora boss is leaving
articles.summary: Bill Peebles, the leader of OpenAI's Sora video generation tool, has announced his departure from the company following its decision to discontinue the Sora project. This move is part of OpenAI's broader strategy to refocus its efforts and avoid distractions in its operations.

articles.title: Should you stare into Sam Altman’s orb before your next date?
articles.summary: Tinder is introducing a feature that allows users to verify their identity by visiting a facial scanning orb, co-founded by OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, in exchange for five free boosts on the app. This initiative aims to enhance user authenticity and follows a successful testing phase.

articles.title: Anthropic’s new cybersecurity model could get it back in the government’s good graces
articles.summary: Anthropic's new cybersecurity model, Claude Mythos Preview, may improve its relationship with the Trump administration, which has previously criticized the company as a national security threat. The model aims to address concerns related to cybersecurity and could potentially help the company regain favor with government officials.
